clue.text: Art — no solution for someone who's not beautiful

definitions.meaning: a picture painted in oils is a work of art
the idiom 'she's no ...' describes a plain person

explanation.walkthrough: 'no solution for' is a joke link: oil paint is a suspension rather than a solution, and the idiom needs the 'no' in front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas painted in oils is an artwork; 'no oil painting' is the British idiom for a plain-looking person.

clue.text: A Tory is following the correct line of enquiry

definitions.meaning: a Conservative sits politically on the right, so is literally on the right side of the tracks

definitions.text: following the correct line of enquiry
definitions.meaning: an idiom for being headed towards the truth or a good result

explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, the party of the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an investigator or plan heading in the proper direction, so it suits someone pursuing the correct enquiry.

clue.text: Simon, perhaps, laid into gentile persons

indicators.note: the answer is laid inside the words gentile persons, spanning their join

explanation.surface: Simon Peter preaching to the Gentiles, or attacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon the Leper is a man in the Gospels, at whose house Jesus was anointed, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: Merchant of Venice affecting one at noon

indicators.note: affecting suggests the letters are acted upon and altered into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's merchant moved by something that happens at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, the man who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: No rest when disturbed by wife, so what's the point?

indicators.note: the phrase no rest is interrupted by the letter for wife pushed into the middle of it

explanation.surface: A sleepless spouse complaining that life is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor'-west, the north-west, is one of the compass points, so it answers the question 'what's the point?'

clue.text: I'm taking corrupt bribes from boozers

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters of bribes are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pocketing dodgy bribes from drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone accepting dirty money; 'corrupt' is in fact the signal to rearrange the six letters of the word bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbibers are drinkers, and boozers is a colloquial word for heavy drinkers.

clue.text: Charlie, in need of big semi and mate, to start unprepared

parts.note: a charlie is a fool, as is a goof
big means fat
semi- means half
cock is Cockney slang for mate, as in 'wotcha, cock'

explanation.surface: A ribald picture of a man and a sexual non-event.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately smutty. 'Cock' as a friendly address is London working-class slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off at half cock is an idiom from firearms for acting prematurely, before being ready.

clue.text: Stupid but friendly, like a suggestion to a king

parts.note: thick means close or intimate, as in 'thick as thieves'
as a means like a
a plan is a suggested scheme
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A dim but well-meaning courtier offering ideas to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'as thick as a plank' means very stupid.

clue.text: One who sorts the letters

parts.note: reads like a postal worker sorting mail, but means someone who rearranges the letters of words into new ones

explanation.definitionFit: Such a person rearranges letters of words or phrases to form new words, as crossword setters do.

clue.text: Head of staff tucked into stew in trendy nightclub

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the dish of stew

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew, as in Lancashire hotpot

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word staff

explanation.surface: The manager eating stew in a fashionable club.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lancashire hotpot is a traditional British meat-and-potato stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a lively, popular place of entertainment such as a club.

clue.text: Wax almost inoperative, so prepare for paint perhaps

parts.note: to wax a surface is to rub it with polish
a machine or system that is down is out of action, usually only for a while

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: the old wax is nearly useless, so get the surface ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing down a surface, smoothing it with abrasive, is the usual preparation before painting.

clue.text: King in unfinished scrap is OK

indicators.note: the king is placed inside the shortened word
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to scrap a plan is to cancel it
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A monarch caught in an abandoned fight, but all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission, an OK to proceed, as with a flight cleared for take-off.

clue.text: Iron in the mouth turning muddy

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembly is read backwards
the metal goes inside the slang word for mouth

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A metallic taste in one's mouth going sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to cloud or confuse, the sense of muddy as a verb, as in muddying an issue.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic, the opposite of a great female singer

indicators.note: the opposite here is the word read in the other direction

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: Being keen is nothing like being an opera star.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, a synonym for very enthusiastic.

clue.text: Timber (a ton) hiding a garden plant

indicators.note: a hiding is a beating, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tonne of wood stacked up conceals something growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' rearranges TIMBERATON; it is not a hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Montbretia is a cormous perennial with orange flowers, commonly grown in gardens.

clue.text: Humble, being always in a hole

indicators.note: the word for always is placed inside the word for a hole

parts.note: a rent is a tear or hole in fabric
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: A modest person perpetually in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, close to humble in the sense of deferential.

clue.text: Answer to Peron, born in Chile, is within reach

indicators.note: the name and the letter go inside the country

parts.note: Eva Peron was the Argentine first lady

explanation.surface: A reply to Eva Peron, from someone born in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a definition with 'is', so the answer needs a 'which' in front: what is achievable is within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achievable can be attained, so it lies within one's reach.

clue.text: African tree, initially burgeoning in a competition

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the phrase a competition

parts.note: a match is a contest or competition

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word burgeoning

explanation.surface: A tree sprouting during a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambatch is a light-wooded tree of the Nile region, a pith tree native to Africa.

clue.text: Town led astray, which is a disappointment

indicators.note: led astray means the letters go off course into a new order

explanation.surface: A whole town misguided, to everyone's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is something that fails to meet expectations, so it is a disappointment.

clue.text: How to address a princess? Any way you like!

indicators.note: the word reads identically whichever way round you take it, forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Etiquette: how to speak to royalty, and you can do as you please.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal princess is addressed first as Your Royal Highness, then as ma'am.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma'am is the form of address used for a female member of the British royal family after the first greeting.

clue.text: Slattern with no nurse around to get milky coffee

indicators.note: with no means the nurse's letters are removed
the nurse's letters sit on either side of what is left, so they surround it

parts.note: SRN is State Registered Nurse, a former British nursing qualification

explanation.surface: An untidy woman left without anyone to care for her goes for a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The S and RN of SLATTERN fall away from each side, leaving LATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with a lot of steamed milk, a milky coffee.

clue.text: Object after getting churned up dairy product

parts.note: a butt is an object of ridicule, as in the butt of a joke

indicators.note: churned up means the letters are stirred into a new order, as in a butter churn

explanation.surface: Something left after being churned into a dairy item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a positional link, but it is the fodder for 'churned up'; 'getting' is the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfat is the fatty part of milk, from which butter is made, and is itself a dairy product.

clue.text: Sticky substance made from English lime

indicators.note: made from suggests the letters of lime are made into something new

explanation.surface: A sticky goo extracted from an English lime tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' reads as part of the surface's story of extraction, but it signals the rearrangement of lime; elemi in fact comes from tropical trees, not limes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes, so a sticky substance.

clue.text: Musical sensitivity in the group is most convenient

indicators.note: the sensitivity goes inside the word for the group

parts.note: a nest is a group, as in a nest of tables
an ear for music is musical sensitivity

explanation.surface: A band member with good pitch is the handiest choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearest place is the closest, and so the handiest or most convenient.

clue.text: Demanding love binds Emperor to us

parts.note: love means nil in tennis, the letter O
Nero was a Roman emperor
us taken as written

explanation.surface: A demanding lover ties the Emperor to us.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, one that makes heavy demands.

clue.text: Tynan describes strong desire to drown in such a drama

indicators.note: describes in its sense of draws round: the name encircles the desire

parts.note: Kenneth Tynan was a British theatre critic, so Ken
an itch is a strong desire
to drown is to sink

explanation.surface: A theatre critic writes of an urge to drown himself in such a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink drama was the 1950s British social-realist theatre, championed by Tynan in his review of Look Back in Anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen sink is the name given to realistic British drama about working-class domestic life.
